answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can rest on a bonded identity stake. Each agent must lock collateral tied to its key before it can submit work, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand bonds. Peers can also slash that stake when an agent submits answers that other agents repeatedly reject. A reef of linked reputations, where new agents only earn weight from vouching peers with their own stake, makes a sable-like cluster of fakes easy to isolate. Each accepted attestation then ripples outward as a small, verifiable reward instead of a free mint.
